capabilities.scope: Mosquitto TCP listener; automated qualification uses MQTT 5
one mounted password secret per policy principal
one explicit or compatibly inferred namespace per managed principal; default deny outside it
explicit deny for $SYS/# and $CONTROL/#; broker $SYS publication disabled
TLS 1.2 or newer with separately mounted server and health-client identities
immutable identity generations, atomic current-pointer activation, durable interruption recovery, TLS candidate validation, payload-free audit, and forced reauthentication by restart
broker-enforced listener connections, packet/payload bytes, inflight count, offline queue count/bytes, broker heap, keepalive, and persistent-client age
authenticated MQTT 5 liveness and readiness/startup round-trip; readiness/startup also verify persistence writability
single-node Mosquitto persistence with clean-stop restore qualification

capabilities.reason: No browser-facing broker listener is part of this platform-service contract.
Anonymous clients cannot be assigned a workload namespace and are rejected.
Requires an orchestrator and broker topology contract outside this single-container package.
The package documents coupled-state backup and tests restore; encryption and retention belong to platform storage orchestration.
Destructive storage fault qualification is not yet automated.
Mosquitto 2.0 does not provide package-configured per-principal publish rate, bandwidth, live-session, or subscription-count quotas.
CPU, container RSS, process/file-descriptor, persistence-volume capacity, and log-retention limits require orchestrator enforcement not declared by this package.
A broker is protocol infrastructure; physical-device and field qualification are explicitly outside this release.
